answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful deposit before it may place trades, with deposits forfeited when a sampled interaction is proven fraudulent. A randomly selected, stake-weighted review panel checks signed transaction receipts and shared history; one bad verdict can ripple through later audits, while repeated honest work builds a meadow of corroborated trust. A sybil operator must fund every identity separately and risks losing those funds, so multiplying accounts becomes costly rather than free at dawn.
